maria_g: FYI I ran the new compaction+paging regression harness against main overnight. Wanted to surface a surprising memory climb pattern.
sam_k: nice, summary?
maria_g: Short version: steady increases in RSS after ~10M tokens on the synthetic long-span workload. Evictions happen but fragmentation prevents reuse — free list grows and we start allocating new slabs.
aj_patel: can you paste the exact command and the log snippet?
maria_g: sure — command I used (docker image: rw-perf:kv-harness-2026-03):

```
./kv_harness --workload long_span_synthetic --tokens 20000000 --compaction-interval 5m --page-size 4k --slab-size 64M --log-level debug
```

log snippet (trimmed):

```
[00:24:12] kvcache: evicting key seq=124567 size=8192
[00:24:12] kvcache: freed_fragment: offset=0x1f400 len=4096 slab_id=12
[00:24:12] kvcache: allocate slab new_slab=15
[00:24:12] kvcache: fragmentation_report free_fragments=214 allocated_slabs=15
[00:24:12] mem: rss=1.8GB
...
[02:11:05] mem: rss=2.4GB
```

maria_g: compaction runs but doesn't consolidate small freed fragments into reusable extents quickly enough, so allocator requests new slabs and memory grows.
kevin_w: is this the same pattern we saw in the kvcache longtail run last month? sounds similar but the slab/fragment sizes differ.
aj_patel: IIRC last month we had a bug in the free-list coalescer that skipped adjacent fragments when offsets were misaligned by a single page. That was patched in patch/kv-coalesce-2026-02, but maybe this workload exposes another edgecase.
sam_k: timeline: can you repro in a short run (like 1M tokens) with verbose fragment dumps? we can attach to heap profile and see fragmentation map.
maria_g: yes repro is quick if you throttle batching to small sizes. I ran a 1.2M token quick run with `--verbose-frag` and saw repeated pattern of 3–6 small fragments per slab that never merge.

perf-bot: Build 9812 finished: benchmark/kv-harness (linux) — artifacts: http://ci.redwood/9812/artifacts/kv-frag-dump

maria_g: attaching a reduced frag dump (link in thread). Observed two hotspots in code: `allocator::split_free_fragment` and `kvcache::evict_async`. Both lock the same mutex in quick succession which could reorder coalescing.
kevin_w: could be a lock ordering / concurrency window: evict_async frees fragments from IO thread while compaction holds the slab mutex. If free fragment deposition is racy we might miss merge opportunities.
aj_patel: proposed short plan:
- add deterministic unit test for adjacent-page coalescing (synthetic allocation pattern)
- instrument free-list to emit coalesce attempts + success/failure counters
- run harness with disabled compaction to isolate eviction-only behavior
- try an eager background compactor that merges fragments every 30s rather than 5m

sam_k: agree. Also let's add a regression test in the nightly suite that runs the long_span_synthetic workload for 2M tokens and fails if RSS growth > 20% over baseline.
maria_g: I pushed a PR with the coalesce counters and a failing unit test that reproduces the pattern locally: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4321
kevin_w: I'll look into lock ordering and see if we can relax notifier hooks so compaction and evict_async don't conflict. If we add a per-slab atomic coalesce pass we can avoid the big mutex.

aj_patel: one more datapoint — when I force page-size=8k the fragmentation disappears (less small fragments) which points to small-page edge.
maria_g: thanks — I'll run the harness matrix with 4k/8k and different slab sizes tomorrow and report back in this thread.

sam_k: next steps actionable: @maria_g run matrix, @aj_patel validate unit test and add to CI, @kevin_w prototype per-slab coalesce change, I'll own adding the nightly regression. Aim for fix in next sprint.
maria_g: ack. Posting results by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
